title: Scalar Implementations
description:
Reference implementations of the functions. They define what each function computes: they are the code of the scalar ISA, the Level 3 fallback of the other ISAs, and the reference of the generated tests. A function can have several entries that split its datatypes or its mask variants.

Checked when the file is loaded: every datatype and mask variant of a declared function is covered by an entry. The entries of an undeclared function get a `dead-code` warning.

implem: res.r[i] = %!pred_cond!% (r0.r[i] > r1.r[i] ? r0.r[i] - r1.r[i] : r1.r[i] - r0.r[i]) %!pred_alt!%;

type.description: `element-wide`: `implem` is the body of a loop over the lanes, written by the generator (`i` is the lane index, `r0.r[i]` a lane of the first argument, `res.r[i]` a lane of the result). `vector-wide`: `implem` is the whole body of the function (reductions, permutations).

datatypes.description: `all_defs` (the datatypes of the interface), an alias of `DATATYPES_MAP` or an explicit list.

variants.description: `[]`: every variant allowed by the `variants` of the function in `registry_interfaces.json`. Otherwise the variants of this entry, among `u` (unmasked), `m` (Merge-Masked), `z` (Zero-Masked) and `s` (Source-Masked).

implem.description: Code, as a string or a list of lines, in the [templating DSL](../templating_dsl.md). `%!pred_cond!%` and `%!pred_alt!%` implement the mask variants.
